howToCalculate.title: How to calculate salary by days worked
howToCalculate.p1: The default estimate divides monthly salary by 30 and multiplies by paid days entered manually or derived from the period helper.
howToCalculate.p2: Paid days are remunerated calendar days in Brazilian payroll, not automatically business days, time-clock punches, or absence classification.

divisor.title: When to use divisor 30 or month days
divisor.p1: Divisor 30 is common for monthly employees and uses CLT article 64 as a reference for monthly divisor in hourly conversion.
divisor.p2: Use month days or a manual divisor when company policy, a collective agreement, or payslip review requires another criterion.

admissionDismissal.title: Admission or dismissal in the middle of the month
admissionDismissal.text: The period helper counts inclusive dates and clips them to the reference month. For full severance, also check the severance calculator.

legalDeductions.title: INSS and IRRF on proportional salary
legalDeductions.p1: When enabled, the estimate applies 2026 INSS/IRRF tables to taxable proportional earnings entered here.
legalDeductions.p2: Other salaries, jobs, and payroll items in the same month can change official withholding.

officialDifference.title: Why the official payslip may differ
officialDifference.text: Official payroll may include absences, DSR, leave, variable averages, taxable rubrics, collective agreements, eSocial, court orders, and internal rounding.

disclaimer.title: Important notice
disclaimer.text: This tool is an educational payroll estimate, not legal, tax, accounting, or official salary advice. The official payslip, payroll/eSocial, employer, collective agreement, court order, and professional review prevail.

q1.question: Does the calculator show the exact payslip amount?
q1.answer: No. It estimates proportional salary from user-entered data; official payroll and employer rules prevail.

q2.question: Should I divide salary by 30 or by the days in the month?
q2.answer: Divisor 30 is this estimate's default convention. Use month days or manual divisor when payroll policy requires another criterion.

q3.question: Are days worked business days or calendar days?
q3.answer: Here they are paid calendar days. The tool does not automatically decide business days, absences, DSR, or medical certificates.

q4.question: How do I calculate salary when admitted mid-month?
q4.answer: Enter monthly salary, month, admission date, and the last paid day of the month, or type paid days manually.

q5.question: How do I calculate salary when dismissed before month end?
q5.answer: Use start and end dates for the worked part of the month to estimate salary balance. For full severance, use the severance calculator.

q6.question: Do INSS and IRRF apply to proportional salary?
q6.answer: They may apply to the taxable base of the payroll month. This version estimates with 2026 tables, but other earnings can change official withholding.

q7.question: Are absences, medical certificates, and DSR included?
q7.answer: Not automatically. Classification of absences, certificates, DSR, and leave depends on payroll, applicable law, and employer policy.
